assignedReviews.card_evidence: Armadillos live only in the Americas — mostly in Central and South America — and nowhere else in the world.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to explain how lines of evidence, such as fossils, biogeography, and comparative morphology, support the occurrence of evolution
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a biogeographic distribution fact about armadillos but does not explain how biogeography supports evolution, which is the core action of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Armadillos live only in the Americas — mostly in Central and South America — and nowhere else in the world.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires classifying Philippine animals/plants by habitat using a drawing or diagram. The card is about non-Philippine armadillos and provides no habitat classification or required representation.

copy.en: Armadillos live only in the Americas — mostly in Central and South America — and nowhere else in the world.
copy.tl: Ang mga armadillo ay nasa Amerika lang matatagpuan — lalo na sa Gitna at Timog Amerika — wala sa ibang bahagi ng mundo.
copy.bis: Ang mga armadillo makit-an lamang sa Amerika — ilabi na sa Tunga ug Habagatang Amerika — wala sa ubang bahin sa kalibutan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the faster a stick is swung, the more force it carries when it strikes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that momentum depends on the mass and the velocity of a moving object that can be used to predict the impact the object will have if it hits another object
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses how swing speed affects force, but the competency requires explaining that momentum depends on mass and velocity and can predict impact. The card does not mention mass, momentum, or the quantitative relationship, so it only touches on the general idea of impact without directly supporting the momentum concept.

copy.en: Arnis is the national sport of the Philippines that uses rattan sticks — the faster a stick is swung, the more force it carries when it strikes!
copy.tl: Ang arnis ay ang pambansang isport ng Pilipinas na gumagamit ng mga patpat na yantok — habang mas mabilis na iindayog ang patpat, mas malakas ang puwersa nito kapag tumama!
copy.bis: Ang arnis mao ang nasudnong dula sa Pilipinas nga naggamit og mga sungkod nga yantok — kon mas paspas iwasiwas ang sungkod, mas kusog ang puwersa niini kon motama!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A very large eruption spreads ash and gas high in the air. This blocks sunlight and cools the planet for a while!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain what volcanoes are and how they are formed
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the climatic effect of a large volcanic eruption (blocking sunlight and cooling), but does not explain what volcanoes are or how they are formed, which is the focus of G6-E-1.

copy.en:
Can a volcano cool down the whole planet?

Yes! A very large eruption spreads ash and gas high in the air. This blocks sunlight and cools the planet for a while!
copy.tl:
Kaya bang palamigin ng bulkan ang buong planeta?

Oo! Ang napakalakas na pagsabog ay nagpapakalat ng abo at gas sa himpapawid. Humaharang ito sa sikat ng araw at nagpapalamig sa mundo nang panandalian!
copy.bis:
Makapabugnaw ba ang bulkan sa tibuok kalibotan?

Oo! Ang kusog kaayo nga pagbuto magkatag ug abo ug gas sa kahanginan. Mobabag kini sa kahayag sa adlaw ug makapabugnaw sa kalibotan sa makadiyot!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many kids with asthma have a doctor's plan telling them exactly what medicine to take every day to prevent attacks.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions asthma, a respiratory condition, but does not identify or describe the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work. It only discusses a doctor's medication plan, which is not the competency's content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many kids with asthma have a doctor's plan telling them exactly what medicine to take every day to prevent attacks.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about asthma management, not about describing how the respiratory system (or any body system) works. It does not provide information on the function of the respiratory system, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en: Many kids with asthma have a doctor's plan telling them exactly what medicine to take every day to prevent attacks.
copy.tl: Maraming batang may hika ang may planong galing sa doktor na nagsasabi kung anong gamot ang iinumin araw-araw para maiwasan ang atake.
copy.bis: Daghang bata nga adunay hubak ang adunay plano gikan sa doktor nga nagsulti kon unsang tambal ang inomon kada adlaw aron malikayan ang pag-atake.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Smoke from cigarettes and pollution makes asthma worse
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a respiratory health effect (asthma worsened by smoke) but does not identify the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or describe how they work, which is the core of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Smoke from cigarettes and pollution makes asthma worse
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things in the environment, such as trash disposal, and burning household materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions smoke (a product of burning materials) causing harm, but it does not explain that changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things, nor does it address trash disposal or burning household materials as the competency requires. The focus is on asthma avoidance, not on material changes.

copy.en: Smoke from cigarettes and pollution makes asthma worse, so kids with asthma should stay away from smoky places.
copy.tl: Ang usok mula sa sigarilyo at polusyon ay nakakapalala ng hika, kaya dapat iwasan ng batang may hika ang mga mausok na lugar.
copy.bis: Ang aso gikan sa sigarilyo ug polusyon makapagrabe sa hubak, mao nga ang bata nga adunay hubak angay molikay sa mga dapit nga daghan og aso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A child with asthma can still play sports actively
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions asthma, a respiratory condition, but does not identify or describe the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work. It only gives lifestyle advice about sports participation, which is not direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: A child with asthma can still play sports actively, as long as the condition is well controlled with medicine!
copy.tl: Kahit may hika ang isang bata, kaya pa rin niyang maglaro at mag-sports nang aktibo kapag maayos itong kinokontrol gamit ang gamot!
copy.bis: Bisan ang bata nga adunay asma makahimo gihapon og dula ug sports nga aktibo kon maayo kining makontrol pinaagi sa tambal!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Signs of asthma include wheezing or whistling when breathing, coughing, and a tight feeling in the chest.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card lists symptoms of asthma (wheezing, coughing, chest tightness) but does not identify the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or describe how they work, which is the focus of G5-L-2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Signs of asthma include wheezing or whistling when breathing, coughing, and a tight feeling in the chest.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions breathing and chest symptoms, which are associated with the respiratory system, but it does not describe how any human body system works, including the respiratory system, as required by G4-L-1.

copy.en: Signs of asthma include wheezing or whistling when breathing, coughing, and a tight feeling in the chest.
copy.tl: Kabilang sa mga palatandaan ng hika ang paghingang parang may hagok, ubo, at masikip na pakiramdam sa dibdib.
copy.bis: Lakip sa mga timailhan sa asma ang pagginhawa nga may sipol nga tingog, ubo, ug gahi nga pamati sa dughan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: most people are simply born with that eye shape
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that genetic information is passed on to offspring from both parents by the process of meiosis and fertilization
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses a misconception about astigmatism (not contagious, not caused by phone use/reading in the dark) and notes that most people are born with the eye shape. It does not explain meiosis, fertilization, or how genetic information is passed from both parents to offspring. The mention of being born with a trait is only tangentially related to genetics and does not directly support the competency's instructional goal.

copy.en:
Is astigmatism contagious?

No! It's usually not caused by phone use or reading in the dark either: most people are simply born with that eye shape.
copy.tl:
Nakakahawa ba ang astigmatism?

Hindi! Karaniwan din itong hindi dahil sa paggamit ng cellphone o pagbabasa sa dilim: ipinanganak lang ang karamihan na may ganoong hugis ng mata.
copy.bis:
Makatakod ba ang astigmatism?

Dili! Kasagaran dili usab kini tungod sa paggamit og cellphone o pagbasa sa kangitngit: natawo lang ang kadaghanan nga adunay ingon niana nga porma sa mata.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because everything floats in space, astronauts eat specially packed food and sleep in sleeping bags strapped down so they don't drift away!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes behavior in space (floating) but does not identify gravity as a non-contact force affecting objects on Earth, nor does it explain predictable effects on Earth. It only tangentially relates to gravity through the absence of its effects in space.

copy.en: Because everything floats in space, astronauts eat specially packed food and sleep in sleeping bags strapped down so they don't drift away!
copy.tl: Dahil lumulutang ang lahat sa kalawakan, kumakain ang mga astronaut ng specially packed food at natutulog sa sleeping bags na nakatali para hindi lumutang!
copy.bis: Tungod kay ang tanan molutaw sa kawanangan, mokaon ang mga astronaut og specially packed food ug matulog sa sleeping bags nga gigapos aron dili molutaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many atolls form when a volcanic island slowly sinks
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the formation of an atoll, a landform, but does not identify local examples of landforms/bodies of water nor describe how they influence living and non-living components as required by G5-E-1. It only shares a general geological process.

copy.en: Many atolls form when a volcanic island slowly sinks, but the coral reef around it keeps growing upward!
copy.tl: Maraming atoll ang nabuo nang dahan-dahang lumubog ang bulkang isla, habang patuloy na tumutubo pataas ang coral reef sa paligid!
copy.bis: Daghang atoll naporma sa dihang hinay-hinay nga nilubog ang bulkanikong isla, samtang padayon nga mitubo paibabaw ang coral reef sa palibot!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It comes from a Greek word meaning "cannot be cut"
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: develop a timeline for the historical background of the development of the current Atomic Model that identifies tiny particles as atoms
assignedReviews.reason: The card only provides the etymology of the word 'atom'. The competency requires developing a timeline for the historical background of the development of the current Atomic Model. This single fact does not support the skill of constructing a timeline or describing the development of the atomic model; it is merely a related historical note.

copy.en:
Where does the word "atom" come from?

It comes from a Greek word meaning "cannot be cut", because people once thought it was the smallest piece of matter!
copy.tl:
Saan galing ang salitang "atomo"?

Galing ito sa Griyego na ibig sabihin ay "hindi na mahahati", dahil dati ay inisip na ito ang pinakamaliit na piraso ng bagay!
copy.bis:
Asa gikan ang pulong nga "atomo"?

Gikan kini sa Griyego nga nagkahulogan og "dili na matunga", kay kaniadto gihunahuna nga kini ang pinakagamay nga tipik sa butang!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Atoms, made of protons, neutrons, and electrons, are the building blocks of matter, and they combine to form molecules like water.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the properties of ionic, covalent, and metallic substances, such as melting point, hardness, electrical and thermal conductivity
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that atoms are building blocks and combine into molecules. It does not address ionic, covalent, or metallic substances, nor their properties (melting point, hardness, conductivity). The content is general chemistry background, not direct support for investigating properties of these substance types.

copy.en: Atoms, made of protons, neutrons, and electrons, are the building blocks of matter, and they combine to form molecules like water.
copy.tl: Ang mga atom, na gawa sa protons, neutrons, at electrons, ay ang building blocks ng matter, at nagsasama-sama sila para makabuo ng molecules tulad ng tubig.
copy.bis: Ang mga atom, nga gihimo sa protons, neutrons, ug electrons, mao ang building blocks sa matter, ug maghiusa sila aron makahimo og molecules sama sa tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Auroras happen very high up, about 100 to 300 kilometers above the ground!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify objects, activities, or natural events observed in their local environment that can be explained by science
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a natural event (aurora) but does not ask students to identify it as a local object/activity/event explained by science, nor does it connect it to the local environment. It only states an altitude fact, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Auroras happen very high up, about 100 to 300 kilometers above the ground!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: Auroras are sky phenomena, but the competency specifically lists the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars as the natural objects to observe and describe. Auroras are not among these, and the card does not involve guided observation or description of these celestial objects. The content is only tangentially related to sky objects.

copy.en: Auroras happen very high up, about 100 to 300 kilometers above the ground! That is much, much higher than any flying airplane.
copy.tl: Nangyayari ang aurora nang napakataas, mga 100 hanggang 300 kilometro sa itaas ng lupa! Mas mataas pa ito kaysa sa anumang lumilipad na eroplano.
copy.bis: Ang aurora mahitabo sa hilabihan ka taas, mga 100 ngadto sa 300 ka kilometro ibabaw sa yuta! Mas taas pa kini kaysa sa bisan unsang naglupad nga eroplano.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It marks the start of autumn, also known as fall!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single seasonal fact (September equinox starts autumn) but does not involve making a Sun-Earth-Moon system model, nor does it explain the observable effects of predictable patterns such as seasons, star patterns, or eclipses. The content is only tangentially related to the seasons component of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It marks the start of autumn, also known as fall!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain, using models, how the tilt of the Earth affects the changes in the length of daytime at different times of the year
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the start of autumn but does not explain, using models, how the tilt of the Earth affects the length of daytime at different times of the year. It provides no information about Earth's tilt, daytime length, or model-based explanation, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What season starts with the September equinox in the Northern Hemisphere?

It marks the start of autumn, also known as fall!
copy.tl:
Anong season ang nagsisimula sa September equinox sa Northern Hemisphere?

Ito ang nagsisimula ng season na autumn, o taglagas!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga season ang nagsugod sa September equinox sa Northern Hemisphere?

Kini ang nagsugod sa season nga autumn, o fall!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Babies are born with about 300 bones, and many fuse together as they grow, leaving adults with only 206.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a fact about the number of bones and their fusion, but does not describe how the skeletal system works (e.g., support, movement, protection). It shares vocabulary with the skeletal system but offers no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
Do babies have more bones than adults?

Yes! Babies are born with about 300 bones, and many fuse together as they grow, leaving adults with only 206.
copy.tl:
Mas marami bang buto ang sanggol kaysa matanda?

Oo! Ang mga sanggol ay ipinapanganak na may mahigit 300 na buto, na unti-unting nagsasanib paglaki nila kaya nagiging 206 na lamang.
copy.bis:
Mas daghan ba og bukog ang masuso kaysa hamtong?

Oo! Ang mga masuso natawo nga adunay mga 300 ka bukog, ug daghan ang naghiusa samtang sila motubo, mao nga mahimong 206 na lang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the baby comes out through the mother's birth canal
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the process of human birth but does not identify which groups of animals give birth to live young versus lay eggs, nor does it mention mammals, birds, or reptiles. It does not directly support the classification skill in the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the mother's birth canal
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the female reproductive system as ovaries, uterus, and vagina and those of the male reproductive system as the prostate, testis, and penis and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the birth canal (vagina) but does not identify or describe the parts of the female reproductive system (ovaries, uterus, vagina) or the male reproductive system, nor does it use pictures or labeled diagrams. It only references one structure in passing, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: In a normal birth, the baby comes out through the mother's birth canal, usually head first.
copy.tl: Sa karaniwang panganganak, lumalabas ang sanggol mula sa daanan ng panganganak ng ina, kadalasang ulo muna.
copy.bis: Sa naandan nga pagpanganak, mogawas ang bata gikan sa agianan sa pagpanganak sa inahan, kasagaran ulo ang una.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A baby pig is called a piglet.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card only provides the name for a baby pig (piglet). It does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants, nor describe stages from birth to adulthood. The term 'piglet' is a vocabulary item related to a life-cycle stage but does not directly support the competency's skill of comparing life cycles.

copy.en:
What do you call a baby pig?

A baby pig is called a piglet.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa anak ng baboy?

Ang anak ng baboy ay tinatawag na biik.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang tawag sa anak sa baboy?

Ang anak sa baboy gitawag og piglet o biik.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Antibiotics are medicines that kill harmful bacteria or stop them from growing and spreading in the body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bacteria but does not teach that bacteria are unicellular or contrast them with multicellular organisms. It only discusses antibiotics as medicines, which is unrelated to the competency's focus on cellular organization.

copy.en: Antibiotics are medicines that kill harmful bacteria or stop them from growing and spreading in the body.
copy.tl: Ang antibyotiko ay gamot na pumapatay o pumipigil sa paglaki ng nakakasamang bakterya.
copy.bis: Ang antibiyotiko tambal nga mopatay o mopugong sa pagtubo sa makadaot nga bakterya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They form endospores—a tough protective coat that lets them survive extreme heat, cold, or hunger for a very long time.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bacteria but does not teach that bacteria are unicellular or contrast unicellular with multicellular organisms. The endospore survival mechanism is unrelated to the competency's focus on cell number.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They form endospores—a tough protective coat that lets them survive extreme heat, cold, or hunger for a very long time.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: Endospore formation is a survival adaptation, but the card does not discuss evolution concepts such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, or adaptation in the context of evolutionary theory. It only describes a bacterial survival mechanism.

copy.en:
How do some bacteria survive extreme conditions?

They form endospores—a tough protective coat that lets them survive extreme heat, cold, or hunger for a very long time.
copy.tl:
Paano nabubuhay ang ilang bacteria sa matinding kondisyon?

Gumagawa sila ng endospore—matibay na balot na nagbibigay-daan sa kanilang mabuhay sa matinding init, lamig, o kagutuman nang matagal.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkabuhi sa uban bacteria sa grabe nga kahimtang?

Naghimo sila og endospore—kusgan nga balot nga motabang kanila mabuhi sa grabe nga init, bugnaw, o kagutom sulod sa dugay nga panahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rhizobium bacteria live inside their roots and turn nitrogen gas from the air into a fertilizer the plant can use!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions roots but does not address observing outer plant parts or the role of roots in absorbing water and nutrients from the soil. It describes nitrogen fixation by symbiotic bacteria, which is a different concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rhizobium bacteria live inside their roots and turn nitrogen gas from the air into a fertilizer the plant can use!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions roots but does not describe the root and shoot system or why they are important. It focuses on bacterial nitrogen fixation, not the structure or function of plant organs.

copy.en:
How do bean plants get natural fertilizer?

Rhizobium bacteria live inside their roots and turn nitrogen gas from the air into a fertilizer the plant can use!
copy.tl:
Paano nakakakuha ng abono ang munggo?

Nakatira ang Rhizobium bacteria sa mga ugat nito at ginagawang abono ang nitrogen mula sa hangin, para magamit ng halaman!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkuha sa balatong og abono?

Ang Rhizobium bacteria nagpuyo sa mga ugat niini ug ginabag-o ang nitrogen gikan sa hangin ngadto sa abono nga magamit sa tanom!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most bacteria have a tough outer cell wall
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bacteria but does not address unicellular vs multicellular organization, so it does not directly support recognizing that some organisms are single-celled.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most bacteria have a tough outer cell wall
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use proper techniques in observing and identifying the parts of a cell with a microscope such as the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and chloroplasts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a bacterial cell wall but does not involve microscope techniques or identifying the listed cell parts (cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, chloroplasts).

copy.en: Most bacteria have a tough outer cell wall that gives them shape and stops them from bursting, though some like Mycoplasma have none.
copy.tl: Karamihan ng bacteria ay may matibay na panlabas na cell wall na nagbibigay hugis at proteksyon laban sa pagputok, pero may ilan tulad ng Mycoplasma na wala nito.
copy.bis: Kadaghanan sa bakterya adunay kusog nga gawas nga cell wall nga naghatag og porma ug proteksyon batok sa pagputok, apan naa'y pipila sama sa Mycoplasma nga wala ani.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most urinary tract infections are caused by E. coli bacteria from the intestines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions intestines and the urinary tract, but it does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, and it does not explain how body systems work together such as digestion and excretion. It only states a UTI fact, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most urinary tract infections are caused by E. coli bacteria from the intestines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card names E. coli as bacteria, but it does not teach the unicellular versus multicellular distinction or give examples of single-celled versus many-celled organisms. The mention of bacteria is incidental to a UTI fact, not instructional support for recognizing unicellular organisms.

copy.en: Most urinary tract infections are caused by E. coli bacteria from the intestines, and they happen more often in women because of their shorter urethra.
copy.tl: Ang karamihan ng urinary tract infection ay dulot ng E. coli bacteria mula sa bituka, at mas madalas ito sa mga babae dahil mas maikli ang urethra nila.
copy.bis: Ang kadaghanan sa urinary tract infection gikan sa E. coli bakterya sa tinai, ug mas sagad kini sa mga babaye tungod sa mas mubo nilang urethra.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the chemical formula for baking soda is NaHCO3
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a chemical formula and common name for baking soda. It does not describe properties of pure substances (fixed chemical composition, elements vs compounds, or unique proton numbers). The formula is a vocabulary-level connection, not instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the chemical formula for baking soda is NaHCO3
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: write the chemical formula and chemical names of some common ionic compounds, including sodium chloride (NaCl), magnesium oxide (MgO), potassium chloride (KCl) and magnesium chloride (MgCl2)
assignedReviews.reason: G9-M-6 requires writing chemical formulas and names of common ionic compounds, with specific examples (NaCl, MgO, KCl, MgCl2). The card gives one formula (NaHCO3) and its name, but does not teach how to write formulas or names, and baking soda is not among the listed compounds. It is only a related example.

copy.en: Did you know the chemical formula for baking soda is NaHCO3? It is also known as sodium bicarbonate!
copy.tl: Alam mo ba na ang kemikal na pormula ng baking soda ay NaHCO3? Ito ay kilala rin bilang sodium bicarbonate!
copy.bis: Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang kemikal nga pormula sa baking soda kay NaHCO3? Kini nailhan usab nga sodium bicarbonate!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An object stays balanced when its center of gravity is over its base!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses balance and center of gravity, which is conceptually related to balanced forces but does not ask students to identify or describe everyday situations demonstrating balanced or unbalanced forces (e.g., box on inclined plane, man standing still, constant velocity, freely falling fruit, accelerating car). It provides no instruction on force balance or Newton's first law.

copy.en: An object stays balanced when its center of gravity is over its base! A lower, wider base makes it harder to tip over.
copy.tl: Nanatiling balanse ang isang bagay kapag ang center of gravity nito ay nasa base! Mas mahirap matumba kapag mas mababa at malapad ang base.
copy.bis: Magpabilin nga balanse ang butang kung ang center of gravity niini anaa sa ibabaw sa base! Mas lisod matumba kung mas ubos ug lapad ang base.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: different colors carry different vitamins!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses healthy eating and vitamin variety from colorful fruits and vegetables. It does not teach students to identify the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter); food is only implied as a general need, and the card's focus is nutrition, not the concept of basic needs.

copy.en: A plate full of colorful veggies and fruit is usually the healthiest — different colors carry different vitamins!
copy.tl: Mas malusog kadalasan ang platong makulay ang mga gulay at prutas — iba't ibang kulay, iba't ibang bitamina!
copy.bis: Mas himsog kasagaran ang platong mabulokon og gulay ug prutas — lain-laing kolor, lain-laing bitamina!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The balete tree has broad green leaves that stay all year
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes the balete's broad evergreen leaves; it does not identify the role of leaves, roots, or stems in getting water and nutrients from the soil, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The balete tree has broad green leaves that stay all year, so it always looks fresh and leafy.
copy.tl: Ang balete ay may malalapad na luntiang dahon na nananatili buong taon, kaya laging mukhang sariwa ito.
copy.bis: Ang balete adunay lapad nga lunhaw nga mga dahon nga nagpabilin tibuok tuig, mao nga kanunay kining morag presko.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A single pangolin can gobble up millions of insects in just one year
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: Eating insects is not grouping animals as herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A single pangolin can gobble up millions of insects in just one year, helping keep nature in balance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Pangolin insect diet is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en: A single pangolin can gobble up millions of insects in just one year, helping keep nature in balance!
copy.tl: Isang balintong lang ay puwedeng kumain ng milyun-milyong insekto sa loob lang ng isang taon, kaya tumutulong itong mapanatiling balanse ang kalikasan!
copy.bis: Ang usa ra ka balintong makakaon og minilyon ka insekto sulod sa usa lang ka tuig, busa makatabang kini sa pagtimbang sa kinaiyahan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some are filled with air to hang up, while others are filled with helium so they float!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air and helium, which are gases, but does not identify that matter exists in three states (solids, liquids, gases) or name the states. It only gives examples of gases without teaching the classification.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some are filled with air to hang up, while others are filled with helium so they float!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe properties of solids, liquids, or gases in terms of shape and volume. It only notes that balloons are filled with air or helium, without discussing shape or volume characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some are filled with air to hang up, while others are filled with helium so they float!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It mentions air and helium but does not connect them to the concept of matter having mass and volume.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: while others are filled with helium so they float!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that helium-filled balloons float, which relates to gravity indirectly, but it does not observe or describe the effects of gravity on the motion of an object. Floating is not explicitly explained as a gravity effect, and no motion is described.

copy.en: At Philippine fiestas and parties, colorful balloons are everywhere! Some are filled with air to hang up, while others are filled with helium so they float!
copy.tl: Sa mga pista at handaan sa Pilipinas, makukulay na lobo ang laging nandito! Ang iba ay hinipan ng hangin para isabit, at ang iba ay may helium para lumutang!
copy.bis: Sa mga pista ug salu-salo sa Pilipinas, kanunay anaa ang mabulukon nga mga lobo! Ang uban gihuypan og hangin aron ibitay, ug ang uban adunay helium aron molutaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Balut is a duck egg kept warm for a while before cooking
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a duck egg, which is an egg-laying animal, but it does not identify groups that give birth vs. lay eggs or compare them. It only provides a specific example of an egg containing an embryo, without teaching the classification skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: so inside you can see a partly grown duck embryo
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows a single stage of a bird's development (embryo inside an egg) but does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants from birth/egg/seed to maturity. It does not support the comparative life-cycle skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: so inside you can see a partly grown duck embryo
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an embryo stage but does not use a flow chart or compare different stages in the life cycle of animals. The format-required activity (flow chart comparing life-cycle stages) is absent, and the content does not directly support comparing stages.

copy.en: Balut is a duck egg kept warm for a while before cooking, so inside you can see a partly grown duck embryo, fed by the egg's yolk and white.
copy.tl: Ang balut ay itlog ng pato na pinapainit muna bago lutuin, kaya makikita sa loob ang nabubuong sisiw na pinapakain ng pula at puti ng itlog.
copy.bis: Ang balut usa ka itlog sa pato nga gipainit una sa dili lutoon, mao nga makita sa sulod ang nagaporma nga sisiw nga gipakaon sa pula ug puti sa itlog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bamboo is a very tall grass with hollow stems
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions stems but does not describe the root and shoot system or why they are important. It does not support observing or describing root/shoot systems.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bamboo is a very tall grass with hollow stems
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions stems but does not describe leaves, roots, or stems and their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. No direct instructional support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bamboo is a very tall grass with hollow stems
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions hollow stems but does not describe specialized structures like rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, or aerial roots. It does not teach the purpose of specialized plant structures.

copy.en:
What makes bamboo so useful?

Bamboo is a very tall grass with hollow stems, one of the fastest-growing plants, and so strong it's used for houses, furniture, and tools.
copy.tl:
Bakit napakagamit ng kawayan?

Ang kawayan ay napakataas na uri ng damo na may guwang na sanga, isa sa pinakamabilis tumubo, at matibay kaya ginagamit sa bahay, muwebles, at kagamitan.
copy.bis:
Ngano hilabihan kapuslanon ang kawayan?

Ang kawayan taas kaayo nga sagbot nga adunay bangag nga punoan, usa sa labing paspas motubo nga tanom, ug lig-on kaayo mao nga gigamit sa balay, muwebles, ug galamiton.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bamboo's long fibers can be turned into paper, cloth, and baskets
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about useful things made from non-living materials. Bamboo is a living plant, not a non-living material. The card does not address non-living materials at all, so it does not support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bamboo's long fibers can be turned into paper, cloth, and baskets
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The competency describes how changes in solid materials (shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, cut) make them useful. The card only states that bamboo fibers can be turned into products; it does not describe any change process or how shaping/pressing/etc. makes bamboo useful. It shares the theme of useful materials but provides no direct instructional support for the specific skill.

copy.en: Bamboo's long fibers can be turned into paper, cloth, and baskets—making it a very useful natural material!
copy.tl: Ang mahahabang hibla ng kawayan ay maaaring gawing papel, tela, at basket—kaya ito'y mahalagang likas na sangkap!
copy.bis: Ang taas nga himaymay sa kawayan mahimong himoon nga papel, panapton, ug basket—busa mapuslanon kaayo kini nga natural nga materyales!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The banana flower, called 'puso ng saging,' is actually eaten as a vegetable
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: Edible inflorescence as food is not leaves/roots/stems taking water and nutrients.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Did you know banana flowers are edible?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Names a flower as food; does not describe pollination, seed production, or propagation.

copy.en:
Did you know banana flowers are edible?

The banana flower, called 'puso ng saging,' is actually eaten as a vegetable in many parts of the Philippines!
copy.tl:
Kinakain ba ang puso ng saging?

Ang bulaklak ng saging na tinatawag na 'puso ng saging' ay kinakain pala bilang gulay sa maraming lugar sa Pilipinas!
copy.bis:
Makaon ba ang puso sa saging?

Ang bulak sa saging nga gitawag og 'puso sa saging' gikaon diay isip utanon sa daghang dapit sa Pilipinas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: potassium, which is important for a healthy heart and muscles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions potassium being important for heart and muscles, but it does not describe how the muscular or circulatory systems work. It provides a nutrient fact, not an explanation of system function.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: carbohydrates that give quick energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions carbohydrates as a source of energy, which relates to food as a basic need, but it does not identify basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. It is a nutritional fact about bananas, not a lesson on basic needs.

copy.en: Bananas are rich in potassium, which is important for a healthy heart and muscles, and carbohydrates that give quick energy — they also have vitamin B6 and fiber.
copy.tl: Mayaman sa potassium ang saging, mahalaga ito para sa malusog na puso at kalamnan, at may carbohydrates na nagbibigay ng mabilis na enerhiya — mayroon pa itong bitamina B6 at fiber.
copy.bis: Dato sa potassium ang saging, importante kini para sa himsog nga kasingkasing ug kaunuran, ug adunay carbohydrates nga naghatag og paspas nga enerhiya — aduna pa kini bitamina B6 ug fiber.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the starch inside changes into sugar
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a chemical change (starch to sugar) but does not explain why physical changes are reversible and chemical changes are irreversible. It provides an example of a chemical change without addressing the reversibility concept, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the starch inside changes into sugar
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a change in a material (ripening) but does not describe chemical properties such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable. It is about a chemical transformation, not the chemical properties listed in the competency.

copy.en: As a banana ripens, its peel turns from green to yellow, and the starch inside changes into sugar — making it taste sweeter.
copy.tl: Habang naghihinog ang saging, nagbabago ang balat nito mula berde tungo sa dilaw, at ang almirol sa loob ay nagiging asukal — kaya ito nagiging mas matamis.
copy.bis: Samtang mahinog ang saging, mausab ang panit niini gikan sa lunhaw ngadto sa dalag, ug ang almidon sa sulod mahimong asukal — mao nga mas motam-is kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the floats on its sides give it balance while it floats on the water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a banca with outriggers not tipping over because the floats give balance. It mentions balance but does not identify or describe balanced or unbalanced forces, nor does it connect the situation to force concepts such as net force, equilibrium, or examples like a box on an inclined plane. The content is about stability/floating, which is only loosely related to the competency's focus on balanced and unbalanced forces.

copy.en:
Why doesn't a banca tip over?

An outrigger boat (banca) does not tip over easily because the floats on its sides give it balance while it floats on the water!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi tumatumba ang bangkang may katig?

Ang bangkang may katig ay hindi madaling tumaob dahil ang mga katig sa magkabilang gilid ay nagbibigay ng balanse sa bangka habang ito ay lumulutang sa tubig!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dili matumba ang bangka nga adunay katig?

Ang bangka nga adunay katig dili dali matumba tungod kay ang mga katig sa duha ka kilid mohatag og balanse sa bangka samtang naglutaw kini sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It pushes water, not air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that when any two objects interact, there are equal but opposite forces exerted between them, which is evident in many practical situations and applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the paddle pushing water and why air is ineffective, touching on interaction and force, but it does not explain equal and opposite forces between two objects. It lacks the explicit Newton's third law concept required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: air is too light to push the heavy boat backward
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air being light, which relates to mass, but it does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. The focus is on force and motion, not the definition of matter.

copy.en:
Does a paddle push air or water?

It pushes water, not air! If you wave a paddle in the air, almost nothing happens because air is too light to push the heavy boat backward.
copy.tl:
Sagwan ba ang nagtutulak sa hangin o tubig?

Tubig ang itinutulak nito, hindi hangin! Kapag iniwagayway mo ang sagwan sa hangin, halos walang mangyayari dahil masyadong magaan ang hangin para itulak ang bangka.
copy.bis:
Ang bugsay ba moduso sa hangin o tubig?

Tubig ang iduso niini, dili hangin! Kung iwarawara nimo ang bugsay sa hangin, halos walay mahitabo kay gaan ra kaayo ang hangin aron iduso ang sakayan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Milkfish, or bangus, are known for having lots of tiny bones in their bodies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Culinary tiny bones are not describing the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

copy.en: Milkfish, or bangus, are known for having lots of tiny bones in their bodies.
copy.tl: Ang bangus ay kilala sa maraming maliliit na tinik sa katawan nito.
copy.bis: Ang bangus ilado sa daghang gagmayng bukog sa ilang lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The milkfish, or bangus, is considered the national fish of the Philippines!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a fact about milkfish being the national fish. It does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups (plants, animals, microorganisms). No direct instructional support for the classification competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The milkfish, or bangus, is considered the national fish of the Philippines!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a Philippine fish but does not use a drawing or diagram to classify animals/plants by habitat (terrestrial, aquatic, aerial). It provides no habitat classification or visual representation, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The milkfish, or bangus, is considered the national fish of the Philippines!
copy.tl: Ang bangus ang itinuturing na pambansang isda ng Pilipinas!
copy.bis: Ang bangus mao ang giila nga nasodnong isda sa Pilipinas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: babies and children get vaccines and checkups to stay healthy and avoid getting sick
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify issues and concerns in the local community and how they could be addressed by science, such as the treatment of waste
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a community health service (vaccines) but does not identify a specific local issue/concern or explain how science addresses it, as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: babies and children get vaccines and checkups to stay healthy and avoid getting sick
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a health practice but does not identify a specific science invention or explain its impact on everyday life, which is the core of the competency.

copy.en: At the barangay health center, babies and children get vaccines and checkups to stay healthy and avoid getting sick.
copy.tl: Sa barangay health center, binabakunahan at tinitimbang ang mga sanggol at bata upang manatiling malusog at maiwasan ang mga sakit.
copy.bis: Sa barangay health center, gibakunahan ug gitiman-an ang mga masuso ug bata aron magpabiling himsog ug malikayan ang mga sakit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: come from the bark of trees such as the cinchona
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about observing the root and shoot system in plants and their importance. The card discusses medicine derived from tree bark, which is neither the root nor shoot system, and does not teach any plant structure or function relevant to this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some medicines, like the one used against malaria, actually come from the bark of trees
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet basic needs. The card mentions a plant product (bark) used as medicine for humans, which is a loose connection to interdependence, but it does not explain any dependency relationship or how living things meet basic needs through the environment. It only states a fact about a medicine's origin.

copy.en:
Where does malaria medicine come from?

Some medicines, like the one used against malaria, actually come from the bark of trees such as the cinchona.
copy.tl:
Saan galing ang gamot sa malaria?

May mga gamot, tulad ng panlaban sa malaria, na nanggagaling sa balat ng ilang puno tulad ng cinchona.
copy.bis:
Asa gikan ang tambal sa malaria?

Adunay mga tambal, sama sa kontra-malaria, nga gikan sa panit sa mga kahoy sama sa cinchona.
